name: Oceanário de Lisboa
tagline: A big indoor aquarium in Parque das Nações, worth the trip on a rainy or family port day

description.short: Lisbon's large public aquarium, built for Expo '98, organised around a central ocean tank viewed from two levels. It is about 7 km from the cruise terminal in Parque das Nações; plan on about half a day including travel.
description.full:
The Oceanário is the best indoor option in Lisbon for families and for wet days, but it is not a quick add-on. It sits about 7 km north-east of the Jardim do Tabaco terminal in Parque das Nações, so budget roughly half a day: 30 to 40 minutes each way plus 90 minutes to two hours inside, which is the museum's own estimate for an average visit.

To get there, walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia station and take a suburban train to Oriente, then walk about 15 minutes through Parque das Nações to the aquarium on the waterfront. A taxi or ride-hail from the terminal takes about 15 minutes in normal traffic and is often the simpler choice for a group of three or four.

The core of the visit is the central tank, which you see from windows on two floors, surrounded by four smaller habitats representing the North Atlantic, Antarctic, temperate Pacific and tropical Indian oceans. The sea otters and penguins are above water, so you see them at the surface as well as below it. Temporary exhibitions (currently Sea Monsters and Submerged Universe) are included in the standard ticket. Takashi Amano's Forests Underwater exhibition closes on 30 September 2026.

Prices depend on your entry slot: adults pay 29.90 euros between 10:00 and 11:30, 27.70 euros from 12:00 to 15:30 and 25.50 euros from 16:00. Buying online gives a further 5 per cent discount. Late morning, on weekends and on rainy days are the busiest times; if your ship leaves late, a 16:00 slot is both cheaper and quieter.

There are cafés and a restaurant on site, and paid lockers on floor 0 for small bags.
description.history: The Oceanário was built as the Oceans Pavilion of Expo '98, the world's fair that marked the 500th anniversary of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India and turned a former industrial and port area into today's Parque das Nações. The American architect Peter Chermayeff designed it to look like a ship moored in the dock, with the whole building organised around a single large tank to express the idea that the world's oceans form one connected system. That idea still runs through the current permanent exhibition, One Planet, One Ocean.
description.significance: It is one of the largest public aquariums in Europe and a landmark of the Expo '98 regeneration of eastern Lisbon, but for a cruise passenger its value is practical: it is entirely indoors, step-free, easy for children and does not depend on the weather. Families who would struggle with Lisbon's hills and cobbles usually find it the least tiring half-day in the city.

directions.general: On the waterfront at Doca dos Olivais in Parque das Nações, about 15 minutes' walk from Oriente station
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7 km north-east, not walkable. The quickest public route is the train from Santa Apolónia station (10 minutes' walk from the terminal) to Oriente, then a 15-minute walk through Parque das Nações. Taxi about 15 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro Red Line or suburban train to Oriente, then about 15 minutes on foot through Parque das Nações. Buses 705, 725, 728, 744, 708, 750, 759, 782 and 794 also serve the area.
directions.parking: Vasco da Gama Shopping Center car park (walking distance), or Parque das Nações public car parks

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open every day of the year

admissionPrices.notes: Prices depend on entry time. Adults (13-64): 29.90 euros (10:00-11:30), 27.70 euros (12:00-15:30), 25.50 euros (16:00-18:30). Children 3-12: 17.70 / 16.60 / 15.50 euros. Seniors 65+: 19.90 / 18.80 / 17.70 euros. Under 3 free. Figures shown are the lowest (late-afternoon) fares. Flexiticket with no fixed date: 41 euros per adult.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: First slot at 10:00 on a weekday, or from 16:00 for the lowest fare and thinner crowds.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Book a timed ticket online (code ONLINE5 gives 5 per cent off). Allow 90 minutes to two hours inside. No flash photography or selfie sticks. Paid lockers on floor 0 for small bags.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 3.5 to 4 hours including travel (30-40 minutes each way) and a 1.5-2 hour visit
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Not walkable from the ship. Train from Santa Apolónia to Oriente then a 15-minute walk, or a 15-minute taxi. The aquarium itself is step-free with ramps and lifts.
tips: Ticket prices fall through the day: adults 29.90 euros at 10:00-11:30, 27.70 euros at 12:00-15:30 and 25.50 euros from 16:00.
Use the code ONLINE5 on the official ticket site for 5 per cent off.
Last entry is 19:00, so a late slot suits ships that sail in the evening; allow at least 45 minutes to get back to the terminal.
Children up to 2 enter free; ages 3 to 12 pay the child rate, and 13-year-olds pay the adult price.
The Oceanário's own estimate for a visit is 90 minutes to two hours; budget half a day overall.
For groups of three or four, a taxi from the terminal (about 15 minutes) saves the station changes and the 15-minute walk from Oriente.
Flash photography and selfie sticks are not allowed inside.
Forests Underwater closes on 30 September 2026; from October the standard ticket covers the main aquarium and the current temporary exhibitions.

highlights: Central ocean tank viewed from windows on two levels
Four surrounding habitats: North Atlantic, Antarctic, temperate Pacific and tropical Indian Ocean
Sea otters and penguins in the above-water sections
Permanent exhibition One Planet, One Ocean
Temporary exhibitions Sea Monsters and Submerged Universe, included in the standard ticket
Forests Underwater by Takashi Amano, open until 30 September 2026
Waterfront setting in Parque das Nações, next to the cable car
facilities: Restaurants and cafés (Submerso, #SeaTheFuture, Zafra Coffee & Bar)
39 paid lockers on floor 0 (larger suitcases cannot be stored)
Ramps and lifts along the whole visitor route
All exhibition content in Portuguese and English

accessibility.mobilityNotes: The visitor route has ramps and lifts and the museum states it complies with European accessibility standards. Priority service for visitors with reduced mobility, pregnant women and people carrying small children. Guide dogs: contact the Oceanário before your visit.
